title: 59% of Americans Get Their News from Social Media
paragraphs: Many Americans now get their news from social media, according to new data from the Pew Research Center.

Pew asked 5,166 adults in the US about their news habits in August 2026. It found that 59% get news from social media at least sometimes. This number is a little higher than in the last few years. About 26% said they often get news from social media, and 33% said they sometimes do. However, 23% said they never get news there.

Facebook is the most popular place for news. About 40% of American adults regularly get news on Facebook. YouTube is second, at 34%. Instagram is third, at 23%, and TikTok is fourth, at 20%. Only 10% get news on X, which used to be called Twitter, and about 9% get news on Reddit. Pew published these results in October 2026.

There are big differences between age groups. Young people are much more likely to get news on Instagram and TikTok. For example, 39% of adults aged 18 to 29 regularly get news on TikTok. However, only 4% of people aged 65 and older do.
TikTok has grown quickly as a news source. In 2020, only 3% of American adults got news there. By 2026, the number was 20%.
There are also differences between men and women. Women are more likely to get news on Facebook and TikTok. Men are more likely to use YouTube and X.
